analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump (line 3) and a new head-side paragraph around lines 1287-1300 on the coordinator chunk path. The supplied units are BASE text for lines 1612-2428, and neither contains the changed hunk, so the added paragraph's lines are not visible in them. The base excerpts are unchanged context covering MTP, sampling, JSON constraints, tool parsers and vision constraints, and the MiMo native path. No code, configuration or control changes are present, so no security control regresses.

The new paragraph describes ChunkBatcher.enqueue dropping a frame when no session sink is bound, and says SendHandle/ChunkSender persist across reconnects. It also says the sink check runs when the enqueue closure executes, so an old request's frame processed after a replacement sink binds still passes the check. It states plainly that this does not enforce request-to-session identity. This is documentation of existing behavior, not new attack surface. It does touch T-008 (plaintext SSE on encryption failure), T-010 (cancellation propagation) and T-053 (replayed or stale authorization across a connection change). The described gap, where a stale request's encrypted chunk could be delivered on a replacement session, is pre-existing and not introduced here. The coordinator decrypts per hop and presumably rejects unknown request IDs, but that contract and the ChunkBatcher, SendHandle, CoordinatorClient+Connection and ProviderLoop+Cancellation sources were not supplied. Integration should check that ChunkBatcher/SendHandle bind request-to-session identity or that the coordinator rejects stale-request frames, and that encrypted chunks carry per-request session keys. I flag this as an unverified contract, not a finding. The documentation accuracy of the claims about those files cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence.
